newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Feb 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Feb 3.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Monday:

* The National Governors Association decided against seeking dramatic changes in a new federal welfare law and instead asked President Clinton and Congress to continue providing benefits for a small group of legal immigrants.
* Scientists say they could decode the full DNA of many disease-causing pathogens within several years, thereby offering new drug and vaccine strategies.
* The number of rapes in the United States dropped to 97,000 in 1995, the lowest number since 1989, according to a report from the Justice Department.

* Some large New York City cultural institutions, including the New York Public Library, have begun or are beginning major fund-raising campaigns, giving smaller arts groups worry that they may lose out.

* Fifty-five illegal Chinese immigrants who were captured on board the Golden Venture freighter remain jailed in the U.S. more than three years after the freighter they were hiding on foundered off the coast of New York City.
* The people of Pakistan vote on Monday to choose between the party of former Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto and that of another former prime minister, Nawaz Sharif.
